sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This visa lets people 18 to 30 years old (inclusive) have an extended holiday in Australia and work here to help fund their trip.

sections.heading: Overview > You must
sections.text:
- have a passport from an eligible country
- be 18 to 30 years old (inclusive)
- apply from outside Australia
- not be accompanied by dependent children
- apply on your own. You can’t include family members in your application
- not have previously entered Australia on a subclass 462 or 417 visa. If you previously entered Australia on a subclass 462 visa, see the second Work and Holiday visa.

If you hold a valid passport issued by China, India or Vietnam, you must participate in a visa pre-application process (ballot) and be randomly selected to apply for a first Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa.

For more information, see New Work and Holiday visa pre-application process.

Help with your visa

If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- do short-term work in Australia to help pay for your holiday
- study for up to 4 months
- travel to and from Australia as many times as you want
- do 3 months of specified subclass 462 work to become eligible for a second Work and Holiday visa

sections.heading: Overview > Cost
sections.text:
Cost concession

From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Papua New Guinea passport holders who lodge a valid first Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa application. See About this visa.

To work out what your visa will cost, use the Visa Pricing Estimator. The estimator does not take into account the other costs.

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text:
For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

To manage high demand and support the long-term sustainability of the WHM program, we are normalising processing timeframes for most WHM visa applications. The average processing time is expected to be around three months. Do not book flights or make travel, work or study commitments until your visa has been granted.

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- do short-term work in Australia to help pay for your holiday
- study for up to 4 months
- travel to and from Australia as many times as you want
- do 3 months of specified subclass 462 work to become eligible for a second Work and Holiday visa

Work

You can do any kind of work on this visa.

Usually, you can only work for the same employer for 6 months.

If the main purpose of your stay is to work, consider a work visa. Explore visa options.

Study

You can study for up to 4 months (17 weeks).

If the main purpose of your stay is to study, consider a Student visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This is a temporary visa. You must enter Australia within 12 months of the date we grant it. We will not extend or defer this timeframe.

The visa’s period of stay starts on the date you enter Australia. Once you have entered you can:

- stay in Australia for up to 12 months
- leave and re-enter Australia as many times as you like in those 12 months

Note:

- If you have dual citizenship and hold more than one passport, you must enter Australia on the passport linked to your Work and Holiday visa grant.
- You do not need to apply for another visa to enter Australia, such as an eVisitor (subclass 651) visa, once you have been granted your Work and Holiday Visa.
- If you apply for and are granted another visa (such as subclass 651 visa) after the grant of your Work and Holiday visa, your Work and Holiday visa (and related work rights) will cease on the date that visa is granted.
- If your first Work and Holiday visa ceased because of the grant of another visa, such as an eVisitor visa, and you entered Australia on that other visa, you will not be able to apply for another first Work and Holiday visa while you are in Australia.

You have another visa

You must only apply for a Work and Holiday visa once you are ready to enter Australia on that visa.

The Work and Holiday visa period will start on the date you enter Australia, regardless of the reason for your visit. This applies even if we have also granted you an Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) (subclass 601).

For more information, see Before you travel.

sections.heading: About this visa > Stay longer
sections.text:
Staying longer

You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa.

Explore your visa options to stay longer in Australia.

You could apply for a second Work and Holiday visa if you are eligible.

Stay longer on a visitor visa

The total time we let you stay in Australia on your first Work and Holiday visa, and then a visitor visa is 12 consecutive months.

We might grant you longer on a Visitor visa if there are exceptional circumstances.

For this visa, exceptional circumstances might be that a close family member in Australia has died or is seriously ill, and you are required to stay in Australia to help or support.

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family
sections.text:
You cannot include family members in your application.

You cannot be accompanied by dependent children while you are in Australia on this visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
(unless exempt)

You might also have to pay for health checks, police certificates and biometrics.

Cost concession

(Concessions apply in limited circumstances).

Cost for eligible Work and Holiday Maker Visa applicants from Papua New Guinea

From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Papua New Guinea passport holders who lodge a valid first Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa application.

We will charge eligible applicants the lower visa application cost during the application process in ImmiAccount. We will recognise eligible applicants by the valid passport from the specified countries used in the application when they apply.

sections.heading: About this visa > Apply from
sections.text:
You must be outside Australia when you apply for this visa and when we decide your application.

You must declare your current location correctly on your Work and Holiday visa application form.

If you change location after you apply

We cannot grant your visa if you come onshore holding another visa, such as a Visitor visa. You must depart Australia for us to grant your Work and Holiday visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Processing times
sections.text:
For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

Your application might take longer to process if:

- you don't fill it in correctly
- you don't include all the documents we need, or we need more information from you
- it takes us time to verify your information

sections.heading: About this visa > Annual visa limit
sections.text:
Every program year we grant a limited number of first Work and Holiday visas to applicants from each eligible country except the United States of America. The program year begins on 1 July and ends on 30 June.

Once this annual limit or 'cap' is reached, we will not grant any more visas. You should wait until the new program year commences on the following 1 July to submit an application.

To find out if applications are open, suspended or closed from your country of passport see Status of country caps.

sections.heading: About this visa > Pre-application process
sections.text:
China, India and Vietnam passport holders must participate in a visa pre-application process (ballot) and be randomly selected to apply for a first Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa.

For more information, see New Work and Holiday visa pre-application process.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
You must comply with all visa conditions and Australian laws.

See the conditions for this visa.

Tax

You must pay taxes when you work in Australia on this visa.

Superannuation

Australia has compulsory superannuation - a retirement savings scheme. Your employer must pay superannuation into your superannuation fund if you earn more than a certain amount.

You can access your superannuation when you leave Australia.

sections.heading: About this visa > Health insurance
sections.text:
We strongly recommend you take out health insurance to cover any unforeseen medical treatment you might need in Australia. You are personally liable for all your healthcare costs while you are in Australia. Insurance can help limit your financial liability.

See what we consider adequate health insurance.

Learn more about health insurance for overseas visitors.

Reciprocal healthcare agreements

Some countries have a reciprocal healthcare agreement with Australia. Find out more from the Department of Human Services about reciprocal healthcare agreements.

sections.heading: About this visa > Travel
sections.text:
You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is in effect.

Time you spend outside Australia after your first entry does not extend the visa's 12-month period of stay in Australia.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa record
sections.text: We will digitally link your visa to your passport. You will not get a label in your passport.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.text: You must meet all of the following eligibility criteria to be eligible for this visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Hold this passport
sections.text:
You must be a citizen of and hold a valid passport from one of these countries:

- Argentina
- Austria
- Brazil
- Chile
- China, People's Republic of
- Czech Republic
- Ecuador
- Greece
- Hungary
- India
- Indonesia
- Israel
- Luxembourg
- Malaysia
- Mongolia
- Papua New Guinea (PNG)
- Peru
- Poland
- Portugal
- San Marino
- Singapore
- Slovak Republic
- Slovenia
- Spain
- Switzerland
- Thailand
- Türkiye
- Uruguay
- United States of America
- Vietnam

Note: China, India and Vietnam passport holders must participate in a visa pre-application process (ballot) and be randomly selected to apply for a first Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa.

For more information, see New Work and Holiday visa pre-application process.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be this age
sections.text:
You must be 18 to 30 years old (inclusive) when you apply.

** You must apply for your visa before you turn 31 years old in Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST)/Australian Eastern Daylight Savings Time (AEDST). The deadline to lodge an application is midnight AEST/AEDST the day before your 31st birthday. This time applies even if you are applying from outside Australia.

Note that AEST/AEDST will be different to when your birthday ends in your country due to time differences between countries.

*** Avoid submitting your application on your birthday, if possible.

We can still grant you the visa if you apply for it at 30 but turn 31 years old before we make a decision. You must still meet all other requirements.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Previous visas
sections.text:
You must not have previously entered Australia on a:

- Work and Holiday visa (subclass 462)
- Working Holiday visa (subclass 417).

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet our education requirement
sections.text:
You must meet our education requirement.

This table presents our education requirements for this visa by country.

Check the visa pages of the Australian embassy in your country for more detail on our education requirement.

Country of passport | Education requirements
Argentina Austria China Czech Republic Ecuador Greece Hungary Indonesia Luxembourg Mongolia Papua New Guinea (PNG) Peru Poland Portugal San Marino Singapore Slovak Republic Slovenia Spain Türkiye Uruguay Vietnam | You must: have a tertiary qualification from a university, college or training centre, or have completed 2 years of undergraduate university study These are acceptable tertiary qualifications: degrees graduate certificates diplomas These are not acceptable tertiary qualifications: Certificates I to IV level qualifications Senior Secondary Certificate of Education
Brazil India | You must have successfully completed at least 2 years of post-secondary study ('post-secondary study' refers to study post Year 12 completion or equivalent).
Chile | You must: have tertiary qualifications from a university, college or training centre, or have completed or been approved to do a third year of undergraduate university study. These are acceptable tertiary qualifications: degrees graduate certificates diplomas/graduate diplomas These are not acceptable tertiary qualifications: Certificate I to IV level qualifications Senior Secondary Certificate of Education
Israel | You must hold a Senior Secondary Certificate of Education and have either: completed military service or be legally exempt from military service
Malaysia | You must: have a tertiary qualification from a university, college or training centre, or have completed 2 years of undergraduate university study. These are acceptable tertiary qualifications: degrees graduate diplomas graduate certificates These are not acceptable tertiary qualifications: advance diploma diploma Certificate I to IV level qualifications Senior Secondary Certificate of Education
Thailand | You must have a tertiary qualification from a university, college or training centre. These are acceptable tertiary qualifications: degrees graduate certificate diplomas These are not acceptable tertiary qualifications: Certificate I to IV level qualifications Senior Secondary Certificate of Education
Switzerland | You must have completed 2 years of study following compulsory schooling.
United States of America | You must have a Senior Secondary Certificate of Education or equivalent.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have this level of English language
sections.text:
You must have at least Functional English.

You have Functional English if you meet one of the following:

- you are a citizen of and hold a valid passport issued by the United Kingdom, the United States of America, Canada, New Zealand or the Republic of Ireland
- you are a citizen of and hold a valid passport issued by Israel and have successfully completed an English Bagrut exam in the level of 3 study units
- you have studied for a certain period at a particular educational institution where all instruction was in English
- you have completed a relevant approved English language test or assessment*.

*You must have undertaken your English language test or assessment within 12 months of submitting your application. This applies even if you received a test score higher than ‘functional English’. We cannot accept a result of functional or higher if the test is older than 12 months at the time of application.

For more information, visit Functional English.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have a letter of support
sections.text:
You must give us a letter of support from your government (or alternative as stated below) if you are from:

- Ecuador
- Greece
- Indonesia
- Malaysia (Good Conduct Certificate)
- Mongolia
- Peru
- Poland
- San Marino
- Slovenia
- Thailand
- Türkiye

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have enough money
sections.text:
You must have enough money to:

- support yourself while you are in Australia and
- leave Australia at the end of your stay.

This is usually about AUD5,000 for your initial stay, plus the fare to where you are going after leaving Australia.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet the character requirement
sections.text: You must meet our character requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Pay your debts to the Australian Government
sections.text: If you or any family members (including those who don't apply for the visa with you) owe the Australian government money, you or they must have paid it back or arranged to pay it back.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Not had a visa cancelled or an application refused
sections.text:
We will consider your immigration history when we make a decision on your application. This means you might not be eligible for this visa if you have had a visa cancelled or refused.

In some circumstances you may still apply for a permanent visa if you have had a visa cancelled or an application refused. See Limitations on applications in Australia.

If applying for a visa from outside Australia, see Can I go to Australia.

If you want immigration assistance, see Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Sign the Australian values statement
sections.text: You must acknowledge the Australian Values Statement that confirms you will respect the Australian way of life and obey Australian laws when you apply for the visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply
sections.text:
Check if applications are still open for the country of issue of your passport.

You can organise health exams or appoint someone to help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Organise health exams
sections.text:
You might need to have health examinations. You can complete them before you apply or you can wait until we tell you to have them.

Find out the examinations you need and how to arrange them if you want to have them before you apply.

Note: China, India and Vietnam passport holders must participate in a visa pre-application process (ballot) and be randomly selected to apply for a first Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa.

For more information, see New Work and Holiday visa pre-application process.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be:

- a registered migration agent
- a legal practitioner, or
- an exempt person.

You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents
sections.text: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also provide a copy of your birth certificate showing both your parents’ names. If you don’t have a birth certificate and you can’t get one, provide a copy of the identification pages of one of these:

- a family book showing both your parents’ names
- government-issued identification
- a court-issued document that verifies your identity

If you have changed your name, provide proof such as:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents > Provide photographs for paper applications
sections.text:
You must provide photographs of yourself if you apply on paper. The photos must be:

- passport-sized
- less than 6 months old
- good quality colour. We don't accept laser copies
- your full face taken against a plain light-coloured background

You can wear untinted prescription glasses. If you wear a head covering for religious reasons, you can show only your face.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Education
sections.text: Provide evidence of your educational qualifications.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > English language
sections.text:
Show us evidence of either of the following:

- You are a citizen of and hold a valid passport issued by the United Kingdom, the United States of America, Canada, New Zealand or the Republic of Ireland.
- Your English level has been assessed as functional by an Australian Adult Migrant English Program service provider

Or show us evidence that you have completed any of the following:

- the English Bagrut exam in the level of 3 study units and you are a citizen of and hold a passport from Israel
- all years of primary school and at least 3 years of secondary school where all instruction was in English
- at least 5 years of secondary school (in or outside Australia) where all instruction was in English
- at least 1 year of full-time study towards an award at an institution in Australia where all instruction was in English
- the part-time equivalent of 1 year of full-time study towards an award at an institution in Australia where all instruction was in English
- 2 years of a full-time studying or training for a degree, higher degree, diploma or trade certificate (in or outside Australia) where all instruction was in English.

Or show us evidence that, in the 12 months before you applied for the visa, you scored:

- an average band score of at least 4.5 based on 4 parts of an International English Language Testing System (IELTS) test
- an overall band score of at least 30 based on 4 parts of a Pearson Test of English (PTE) Academic
- an overall band score of at least 147 based on 4 parts of a Cambridge C1 Advanced test
- a total band score of at least 32 based on the 4 test components of speaking, reading, writing and listening of a Test of English as a Foreign Language internet-based test (TOEFL iBT).

- Please note that we will only accept a TOEFL iBT if taken on or before 25 July 2023.

For more information, see Functional English.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Government support
sections.text:
You must obtain a letter of support from your government (or alternative as stated below) before lodging your visa application if you are from one of the following countries:

- Ecuador - Ministry of External Relations and Human Mobility
- Greece - Ministry of Education, Research and Religious Affairs
- Indonesia - Directorate General of Immigration
- Malaysia (Good Conduct Certificate) - Malaysian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
- Mongolia - Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mongolia
- Peru - Ministry of Foreign Affairs
- Poland - Ministry of Family, Labour and Social Policy
- San Marino - Ministry of Foreign Affairs
- Slovenia - Ministry of Foreign Affairs
- Thailand - Department of Children and Youth
- Turkey - Ministry of Foreign Affairs

You do not need to provide a letter of support from your government if you are from:

- Austria
- Argentina
- Brazil
- Chile
- China, People's Republic of
- Czech Republic
- Hungary
- India
- Israel
- Luxembourg
- Papua New Guinea
- Portugal
- Singapore
- Slovak Republic
- Spain
- the United States of America
- Uruguay
- Vietnam

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Enough money for your stay and to leave
sections.text:
Provide evidence you have enough money for your stay in Australia. This is usually AUD5,000.

You must also show us you have enough money to buy a ticket to leave Australia at the end of your stay, or that you already have the ticket.

If you don’t attach evidence to your application, processing may be delayed if we need to contact you to request further information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Character documents
sections.text:
We might ask you to provide:

- an Australian police certificate if you have spent a total of 12 months or more in Australia in the last 10 years since you turned 16. We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates issued by the Australian Federal Police. We do notaccept standard disclosure certificates or national police certificates issued by Australian state or territory police
- an overseas police certificate from every country, including your home country, where you spent a total of 12 months or more in the last 10 years since you turned 16
- military service records or discharge papers if you served in the armed forces of any country

We will let you know if you need to give us these documents.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Tell us you are getting help
sections.text:
To nominate someone to:

- receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > For online applications > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Provide original and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating

These details must be in English.

Note: You do not need to have any documents certified.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > For online applications > Scan or photograph
sections.text:
Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.

The scans and photos must be clear.

If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > For online applications > Attach
sections.text:
Attach a document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing.

Learn more about attaching documents.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > For paper applications > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Provide original and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating

These details must be in English.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > For paper applications > Certify
sections.text:
Do not certify police certificates. You need to send us the originals.

Have all other documents certified. This includes:

- non-English documents
- English translations

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > For paper applications > Keep
sections.text: Keep a copy of your completed application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > For paper applications > Send
sections.text:
Send us:

- original police certificates
- certified copies of all other documents
- as much information as possible to help us decide on your application
- each document only once, even if you are using to show more than one thing
- all documents with your application, if you can

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa
sections.text: Applicants must apply for this visa online. Learn how to apply for the visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply online
sections.text:
Apply online if you hold a passport from:

- Argentina
- Austria
- Chile
- China, People’s Republic of
- Czech Republic
- Ecuador
- Greece
- Hungary
- India
- Indonesia
- Israel
- Luxembourg
- Papua New Guinea
- Malaysia
- Peru
- Poland
- Portugal
- San Marino
- Singapore
- Slovenia
- Slovak Republic
- Spain
- Thailand
- Turkey
- United States of America
- Uruguay
- Vietnam

- Log in or create an ImmiAccount.
- Attach documents.
- Pay the application fee. We will not process your application until you pay the fee.
- Note the transaction reference number.

Note: China, India and Vietnam passport holders must participate in a visa pre-application process (ballot) and be randomly selected to apply online for a first Work and Holiday (subclass 462) visa.

For more information, see New Work and Holiday visa pre-application process.

Applicants with dependent children

You can’t apply online if you are the parent of a child under the age of 18.

Work and Holiday visa holders cannot be accompanied by dependent children at any time during their stay in Australia. While it is possible to obtain a Work and Holiday visa if you have a child, your child cannot join you in Australia at any time while you are on your Work and Holiday visa – not even for one day.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
See what you can and must do after you apply.

We will let you know when we have received your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel
sections.text: Do not arrange to travel to Australia until we let you know, in writing, that we have granted you the visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Biometrics
sections.text: We might ask for biometrics. We will let you know if you need to provide them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text: If you didn't have health examinations before you applied, we will let you know if you need them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Attach more information
sections.text:
If you didn't attach all documents when you applied, attach them via ImmiAccount as soon as you can.

We might also ask you to provide more information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Let us know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application.

Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers and attach it in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Help with your application
sections.text:
Let us know if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.

For more information, see Who can help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Tell us if things change after you lodge your application but before we have made a decision.

Things you need to let us know about include:

- you want to withdraw your application
- changes to your passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will let you know our decision in writing.

If we grant your visa, we will tell you:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions.

Keep a copy of the decision notification with you when in Australia.

If we refuse your visa, we will tell you:

- why we refused the visa
- if you have a right to a review of the decision.

Step Summary

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Outside Australia
sections.text:
Before you travel

You must only apply for a Work and Holiday visa once you are ready to enter Australia on that visa. Once we grant your Work and Holiday visa, you can use the visa to enter Australia.

After we grant your Work and Holiday Visa you do not need to apply for another visa, such as an eVisitor (subclass 651), a Transit (subclass 771), or an Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) (subclass 601) visa to enter Australia.

If we grant you an eVisitor or Transit visa after your Work and Holiday visa

If we grant you another visa (such as an eVisitor or Transit visa) after the grant of your Work and Holiday visa, your Work and Holiday visa (and related work rights) will cease as soon as we grant that other visa.

If your first Work and Holiday visa ceased due to the grant of another visa, such as an eVisitor or Transit visa, and you entered Australia on that other visa, you will not be able to apply for another first Work and Holiday visa while you are in Australia.

If we grant you an Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) (subclass 601) visa

If you enter Australia after the grant of your Work and Holiday visa, the 12-month period of stay on your visa will automatically start on that day.

The Work and Holiday visa period will start regardless of the purpose of your visit, even if:

- you just want to transit through Australia on your way to another country

or

- we have granted you an Electronic Travel Authority (ETA) (subclass 601) visa.

An ETA grant will not cease your Work and Holiday visa.

An ETA cannot be in effect at the same time as your Work and Holiday visa. When you enter Australia your Work and Holiday visa will commence. Your ETA will come into effect after the Work and Holiday visa ceases.

Check your travel documents are up to date

- Your Work and Holiday visa will be linked to the passport you declared on your application. If you obtain a new passport after your visa is granted, you must tell us your new passport details. See how to tell us if your situation changes.
- If you do not update your passport details, you will face delays at your overseas departure point and may not be permitted to board your flight.

You must:

- have a Work and Holiday visa that is in effect to enter Australia. You do not need a separate visa to enter Australia. We recommend that you keep a copy of your grant letter (electronic or paper) while travelling
- hold a valid passport issued by a Work and Holiday participant country
- enter Australia using the passport linked to your WHM visa grant. This applies even if you have dual citizenship and hold more than one valid passport.

At the border

Completing an Incoming Passenger Card

All people arriving in Australia must complete the Incoming Passenger Card. You will be given this card onboard.

Leaving the airport faster

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport, if you have one. You may be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
With this visa you can:

- have a holiday
- do any kind of work
- study for up to 4 months
- travel to and from Australia as many times as you want
- undertake 3 months of specified subclass 462 work to become eligible to apply for a second Work and Holiday visa

Work

Usually, you can only work for the same employer for 6 months.

To see your conditions for work, use VEVO.

You must pay taxes when you work.

When you work in Australia, you are protected by Australian workplace law. See information for migrant workers and your workplace rights and entitlements.

Superannuation

If you earn over a certain amount, your employer must pay superannuation into your superannuation fund. Australia has compulsory superannuation - a retirement savings scheme.

When you leave Australia, you can access your superannuation.

Study

You can study for up to 4 months (17 weeks).

To see your study entitlements use VEVO.

Travel

You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is in effect.

Time spent outside Australia after your first entry does not extend the visa’s 12-month period of stay in Australia.

How long you can stay

This is a temporary visa. You must enter Australia within 12 months of the date we grant it.

The visa starts on the date you enter Australia. Once you have entered and the visa stay period starts, you can:

- stay in Australia for up to 12 months
- leave and re-enter Australia as many times as you like in that 12 months.

Stay longer

You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa.

You must apply for a new visa if you want to stay longer.

You could apply for a second Work and Holiday visa if you are eligible.

See your options.

What you must do on this visa

You must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws.

See your conditions in your visa grant letter or VEVO.

Prove you have a visa

To prove you have a visa and show your conditions to someone, use VEVO.

Request your international movement records to get proof of your travel in and out of Australia.

Tell us if things change

Things you need to let us know about include:

- changes to your passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child

See how to tell us if your situation changes.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

Check your travel documents

You must have a valid passport or other travel document to leave Australia.

At the border

Departures SmartGate

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You may be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGate.

After you leave

Getting your superannuation

You are likely to have some money in a superannuation fund if you worked in Australia and you are:

- aged 18 years or older
- paid AUD450 or more before tax in a month

See how to access your super.

Proving you have been to Australia

Request your international movement records to get proof of your travel in and out of Australia.
